question: Assume today is 2026-09-11. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total number of passengers who used public transport in Spain in August 2026 (urban, interurban and special/discretionary transport combined), as it will be first reported in the provisional data of the National Statistics Institute's (INE) Passenger Transport Statistics (Estadística de Transporte de Personas).

target.what: Total passengers carried by public transport in Spain (urban, interurban, and special/discretionary transport combined) during August 2026, as first reported in INE's Estadística de Transporte de Personas (Passenger Transport Statistics) provisional data; counted as passenger journeys/trips (each bo
target.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE), Estadística de Transporte de Personas (ETP)
target.cadence: Monthly, provisional data released roughly two months after the reference month (August data typically published in October)
target.caveats: Working interpretation: total passengers (viajeros) across all three transport classes (urbano, interurbano, especial y discrecional) as reported in the ETP monthly table, counting passenger boardings rather than unique individuals. Alternative interpretations: (a) passengers transported by all mode

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 total passengers can be projected from the ETP monthly series: August 2025 level plus trend growth plus any August-specific seasonal factor. The ETP publishes monthly totals by transport class; the August value in prior years anchors the level and the July-to-August seasonal ratio anchors the shape.
candidates.data_to_find: INE ETP monthly total passengers (viajeros) for all transport classes combined, for August 2023, August 2024, August 2025, and the most recent months before the cutoff (e.g., Jan-Jul 2026 if published). Also the July-to-August ratio in each year. Minimum evidence: August 2025 total and the 2024-2025 August growth rate.
search_hints: Estadística de Transporte de Personas INE viajeros agosto 2025
INE ETP serie mensual viajeros transporte urbano interurbano especial
passenger transport statistics Spain August total passengers

candidates.hypothesis: Total = urban + interurban + special/discretionary passengers. Each component has its own trend and seasonality; summing separately estimated components reduces error versus a single aggregate projection. Urban and interurban are dominated by bus and metro; special/discretionary is dominated by bus charter and school/works services (seasonally low in August).
candidates.data_to_find: ETP monthly passenger totals split by class (urbano, interurbano, especial/discrecional) and by mode (autobús, metro, ferrocarril) for August 2024 and August 2025, plus recent 2026 months. Minimum evidence: August 2025 split by class and the 2024-2025 growth per class.

candidates.hypothesis: Metro Madrid, Metro Barcelona, EMT Madrid, TMB Barcelona and other large operators publish monthly passenger counts that are the dominant urban component. Aggregating major operator August 2026 (or August 2025 with growth) figures and scaling to national urban total via their historical share constrains the urban component.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly passenger counts for Metro Madrid, Metro Barcelona, EMT Madrid, TMB, and other large urban operators for August 2025 and any 2026 months available before cutoff; their share of national urban ETP passengers. Minimum evidence: August 2025 passengers for the top 3-5 operators and their combined share of ETP urban total.

candidates.data_to_find: Renfe monthly passengers (Cercanías, Media Distancia, Avant, AVE if included) for August 2025 and 2026 months before cutoff; share of ETP interurban/urban rail. Minimum evidence: August 2025 Renfe Cercanías + MD passengers.

Spain population ~48-49 million; average monthly trips per capita from ETP history gives a cross-check on the aggregate.

Minimum evidence: annual ETP passengers per capita and August seasonal index.

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 passenger totals are affected by calendar (number of weekdays vs weekends), heatwaves, wildfire disruptions, strikes, and fare policies (e.g., free/reduced Renfe Cercanías passes, subsidised bus fares). These shift the August 2025-to-2026 growth rate away from trend.
candidates.data_to_find: August 2026 calendar (weekday count), any major transport strikes or disruptions in August 2026, heatwave/wildfire events, and status of national free/reduced public transport fare schemes in 2026. Minimum evidence: confirmation of fare-subsidy policy status and any major August 2026 disruption.

a1.role: year-on-year growth factor of total public transport passengers, August 2026 vs August 2025

methods.rationale: Anchors on the reported August 2025 total (362.4M, p65/p71) and applies a modest 2026 growth factor informed by the February 2026 slowdown (p17, p18) and 2025 monthly growth (p34, p38, p41). Shared dependency: both the level and growth rest on INE ETP; failure mode is a large revision to August 2025 or a 2026 rebound not captured by February data.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
